ChaCha RNG state setup, buffer refill, and shared-memory lifecycle helpers.

# Purpose
`fd_chacha_rng.c` implements the life-cycle and buffer refill logic for a ChaCha-based random number generator state object. It defines the required alignment and memory footprint helpers, then provides [`fd_chacha_rng_new`](<#fd_chacha_rng_new>), [`fd_chacha_rng_join`](<#fd_chacha_rng_join>), [`fd_chacha_rng_leave`](<#fd_chacha_rng_leave>), and [`fd_chacha_rng_delete`](<#fd_chacha_rng_delete>) to manage an instance in caller-supplied shared memory. These functions validate the input pointer, check alignment, clear storage, set the generator mode, and erase state on delete. The file also includes [`fd_chacha20_rng_init`](<#fd_chacha20_rng_init>), which copies the key into the generator state, resets buffer offsets, and starts the first refill.

The file also contains the sequential refill path used to extend the internal output buffer with ChaCha blocks. The static helper [`fd_chacha_rng_refill_seq`](<#fd_chacha_rng_refill_seq>) computes the next block index from the current fill position, builds a nonce from that index, and calls a block function to write encrypted output into the ring buffer. The public wrappers [`fd_chacha8_rng_refill_seq`](<#fd_chacha8_rng_refill_seq>) and [`fd_chacha20_rng_refill_seq`](<#fd_chacha20_rng_refill_seq>) select `fd_chacha8_block` or `fd_chacha20_block` as the block function, so the same refill logic supports both ChaCha8 and ChaCha20 variants.
